We introduce a data-driven approach to localize sound sources within video frames, utilizing only audio-visual metadata without requiring actual camera views. Our method trains separate deep neural networks for head and body segments, leveraging an image retrieval strategy that uses appearance-based features to identify matching visual clips from a database constructed from all possible audio-visual scene combinations. This database is automatically generated using dialogue turns in conversational data to extract synchronized audio-visual snippets. Notably, our model needs no task-specific adaptation; it generalizes directly to two distinct datasets—conversational and call-center interactions—with precise localization of human torsos and heads.

Graph neural networks (GNNs) are increasingly utilized to analyze and forecast the behavior of complex systems represented as graphs. A fundamental challenge with current GNN approaches is their reliance on Euclidean aggregation functions, which fail to incorporate the intrinsic properties of data containing significant Lorentzian structure. In this work, we present a novel framework of Lorentzian GNNs designed for general Lorentzian manifolds. We demonstrate that employing the natural metric within the manifold as the affinity function effectively generates robust node representations. We evaluate the efficacy of these Lorentzian GNNs by evaluating them on node classification tasks across three diverse datasets, each endowed with distinct Lorentzian structures, demonstrating superior performance compared to state-of-the-art baseline methods.

This study examines the irreverse problem involving coupled elastic and acoustic systems, specifically focused on identifying a variable thickness of a partition separating a elastic domain from an fluid one. Traditional literature has typically modeled such thickness variations through variable angles; however, this research adopts a variable thickness formulation to enable more drastic configuration changes in the liquid-elastic interface. The specific goal involves retrieving initial conditions required to revert the forward problem, which involves variable thickness coupling. To characterize uniqueness for this reverse problem, variational formulation is employed. Furthermore, based on a stability estimate, existence and uniqueness of the solution are secured under the assumption that the initial subproblem, defined exclusively within the elastic region, possesses its own unique solvability.

We introduce an efficient exponential utility function that generalizes standard UDD (undiscounted delay utility) to manage time preferences. This new framework, which we term TEDD (Trecha efficient delay discounting), incorporates a parameter $\alpha$ to reflect varying levels of impatience. When $\alpha = 1$, the model reverts to traditional UDD; values where $\alpha < 1$ signify hyperbolic impatience, while $\alpha > 1$ signifies hypo-impatience. We examine how TEDD shapes intertemporal choices, revealing a direct relationship between $\alpha$ and the most distant point an agent is willing to wait. Additionally, we demonstrate that the framework aligns with an impatience curve, where $\alpha$ functions as the Tal parameter within a Tsallis-like structure.

We analyze a minimal extension of the scoto-seesaw mechanism featuring a singlet scalar and an additional sterile neutrino, where both new components contribute to generating neutrino masses. Within this model, the Higgs sector becomes less stable compared to the standard scoto-seesaw setup; however, the introduction of the new neutrino simultaneously offers a solution by ensuring the Vev-neutrino correlation aligns with experimental observations. Phenomenologically, the model exhibits WIMP dark matter characteristics driven by freeze-out annihilation into either charged leptons or neutrinos. We map out the parameter space constrained by current data, which includes flavor oscillation experiments, neutrino mass constraints, Higgs coupling deviations, dark matter direct detection results, and precision electroweak measurements. Furthermore, we explore the model's potential signatures at future high-energy colliders.

The crystal field splitting between $e_g$ and $t_{2g}$ $d$-orbitals in 4d and 5d transition metal compounds is substantially larger than in 3d analogues due to enhanced spin–orbit coupling and ligand field effects. While this general trend holds for many 4d and 5d oxides, it can be reversed in specific 4d and 5d spinels, where $e_g$ orbitals become the lower-energy state relative to $t_{2g}$ orbitals. This unique $e_g$-$t_{2g}$ blending is driven by a contraction of the $e_g$ orbitals directed toward the cation, which weakens their interaction with $p$-orbitals of the anion. This study offers a fresh perspective on the unusual electronic structure of 4d and 5d spinels.

Illness-aware image modification (IIM) adapts natural images to depict corresponding synthetic or real pathology. This paper introduces the first Illness-aware Chest X-ray Image Modification (ICIX-IIM) dataset, generated via conditional generative adversarial networks (cGANS) using conditional implicit latent variables (CILs). Unlike standard conditional GANS, cGANS enables multiple diseases to be encoded within a single CIL, allowing one to transform healthy images into diseased states by injecting specific CILS. We propose an implicit conditional GANS (iCIGANS) model to train on IICIX-IIM, demonstrating through experiments that iCIGANS produces more realistic and diverse lesions compared to existing methods. Furthermore, we establish a new protocol by treating conditional implicit latent variables (CILS) as illness-specific disease embeddings. Experiments confirm that models trained on iCIGANS achieve a 10.83% higher diagnostic accuracy for diseases linked to their training CILS, and a 5.20% improvement for diseases present during both training and testing.

ViDaExpert functions as an intuitive software solution designed for the visualization and analysis of multidimensional vector data. With a focus on representing high-dimensional information through techniques like nonlinear manifold learning, it streamlines workflows for both machine learning models and traditional "bag of features" approaches. Specifically tailored for experienced practitioners handling complex machine outputs, the tool manages data comprised of header names, component values, and associated metadata. To facilitate deeper insights, ViDaExpert enables users to sort, filter, and sort through data entries efficiently. Additionally, it supports the display of diverse metadata attributes via tabular formats and graphical elements such as pie charts, bar graphs, and scatter plots. The system also facilitates direct engagement with distributed machine results by allowing interactive comparison and expansion of specific subsets along individual feature dimensions.
